title: Highest-Protein Foods: Ranking Per 100 Grams

seo.title: Highest-Protein Foods per 100 Grams: Ranked
seo.meta_description: See which foods contain the most protein per 100 grams, why cooked and raw values differ, and how the ranking changes by serving and calories.
seo.search_intent: Informational: identify protein-dense foods and understand how to compare them accurately.

excerpt: Aged cheeses, certain seeds and cooked lean meats are among the most protein-dense everyday foods per 100 grams. But serving size, calories and water content can completely change which foods are most useful in practice.
content_html:
Ask which foods have the most protein and chicken breast, eggs and tuna usually come to mind. They are all useful protein sources, but a strict per-100-gram ranking produces a more complicated list. Aged Parmesan and some seeds can match or exceed many meats.

That does not automatically make them better protein foods. A 100-gram comparison measures concentration. It does not account for a normal serving, total calories, sodium, fat, fiber or whether the food is dry, raw or cooked.

Protein ranking per 100 grams

FoodApprox. protein per 100 g
Parmesan cheese35–36 g
Hulled hemp seeds31–32 g
Cooked chicken breast31 g
Pumpkin seeds30 g
Cooked turkey breast29–30 g
Lean cooked beef26–29 g
Lean cooked pork loinabout 27 g
Peanuts25–26 g
Canned tuna, drained24–26 g
Sardines24–25 g
Cooked salmon22–25 g
Almondsabout 21 g
Tempehabout 20 g
Cooked soybeansabout 18 g
Whole egg12–13 g
Cottage cheese11–13 g
High-protein plain Greek yogurt9–11 g
Cooked lentilsabout 9 g
Cooked chickpeas8–9 g

These are representative values rather than guarantees for every product. Cuts of meat, fish species, moisture, brands and cooking methods all matter.

Why dry and cooked foods should not be mixed carelessly

Lentils are an excellent example. USDA-derived composition data put dry mature lentils at about 24.6 g of protein per 100 g. The same database entry for boiled lentils is about 9.0 g per 100 g.

Lentil formProtein per 100 gWater per 100 g
Dry24.6 g8.3 g
Boiled9.0 g69.6 g

Cooking has not erased most of the protein. Lentils absorb water, become heavier and dilute the protein across a larger cooked weight. Meat often moves in the opposite direction: it loses water during cooking, so protein becomes more concentrated per 100 grams.

Serving size changes the answer

Hemp seeds contain roughly as much protein per 100 grams as cooked chicken breast, but a realistic serving of seeds may be one ounce or a few tablespoons. A chicken portion can easily weigh five or six ounces. The meal therefore delivers far more protein from the chicken even though the concentration looks similar.

FoodIllustrative servingApprox. protein
Cooked chicken breast150 g46 g
Cooked turkey breast150 g43–45 g
Drained canned tuna120 g29–31 g
Tempeh150 g30 g
Cooked lentils200 g18 g
Parmesan30 g10–11 g
Hemp seeds30 g9–10 g
Almonds30 g6–7 g
Large egg1 egg6–7 g

Which animal foods are highest in protein?

Cooked lean poultry, lean beef and pork, tuna and many other fish are especially concentrated. Aged cheese can rank even higher by weight because much of its water has been removed during production and aging.

That concentration comes with context. Parmesan, for example, also concentrates fat, calories, calcium and sodium. The food with the largest protein number is not necessarily the food you would want to eat in the largest portion.

Which plant foods are highest in protein?

Seeds, peanuts and some nuts dominate a per-100-gram list, while soy foods stand out when practical portions are considered. Tempeh can provide around 20 g per 100 g and works naturally as the main protein component of a meal. Beans and lentils are less concentrated once cooked, but a cup-sized serving still contributes meaningful protein plus fiber and other nutrients.

What about protein per calorie?

This is a different ranking again. Seeds, nuts and aged cheese are calorie-dense. Lean poultry, many fish, low-fat Greek yogurt, cottage cheese and egg whites provide a greater share of their calories from protein. If the goal is high protein without a large calorie load, protein per calorie can be more useful than protein per 100 grams.

It is still not a complete measure of food quality. Salmon may deliver fewer grams of protein per calorie than extremely lean fish, for example, while contributing long-chain omega-3 fats. Lentils provide less protein per calorie than chicken but also provide substantial fiber.

How much protein do adults need?

Protein needs vary. European Food Safety Authority reference values use 0.83 g per kilogram of body weight per day as the population reference intake for adults. In the United States, individual needs and recommended intakes are also expressed relative to body size and life stage. Athletes, older adults, pregnancy and some medical situations may warrant different targets.

The useful way to read a protein ranking

Use the per-100-gram number to compare concentration, then ask three more questions: How much of this food will I actually eat? How many calories come with that portion? What else does the food contribute?

Once those questions are included, there is no single winner. Lean meats and fish are highly efficient protein sources; soy foods and legumes bring strong plant-based options; dairy can be convenient; and nuts and seeds add smaller but nutritionally useful amounts.

Frequently asked questions

Does chicken have more protein than lentils?

Per 100 g as eaten, yes. Cooked chicken breast is around 31 g, while boiled lentils are about 9 g. Dry lentils are about 24.6 g, but they absorb a large amount of water during cooking.

What plant food has the most protein?

Several seeds exceed 30 g per 100 g, but soy foods such as tempeh are often more practical as the main protein in a meal. Legumes add protein along with fiber.

Should I compare raw or cooked values?

Compare foods in the form you actually eat and label the state clearly. Water loss or gain during cooking can alter the per-100-gram number dramatically.

faq.question: Does chicken have more protein than lentils?
faq.answer: Cooked chicken breast is about 31 g per 100 g, compared with about 9 g for boiled lentils. Dry lentils are about 24.6 g before they absorb cooking water.

faq.question: What plant food has the most protein?
faq.answer: Some seeds exceed 30 g per 100 g. Tempeh and other soy foods are often more practical as a main protein source because larger servings fit naturally into a meal.

faq.question: Should protein foods be compared raw or cooked?
faq.answer: Use the form normally eaten and state it clearly. Cooking changes water content and therefore the nutrient concentration per 100 g.
